My name doesn't matter much — I've been working these 4.1 mu for 40 years now, same as my mother before me. Let me think about this year.

My wheat goes in the ground in October and I bring it out in June. Then maize goes right in — no time to waste, the season is short. This is how everyone around here does it, and it's how I've always done it.

For wheat, I'll buy the improved seed from the dealer in town — maybe Jimai or Shimai, whatever he has in good bags. Costs more than saving my own but the yield is better, my neighbors all switched years ago. I sow about 15 kg of seed per mu since I plant a bit thick — soil here is heavy and some seedlings always die over winter.

Fertilizer — this is where the money goes. For wheat I'll put down a bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before sowing, that's one 50 kg bag per mu. Then in spring when I irrigate the green-up water, I top-dress with urea, about 15 kg per mu. So all told maybe 25 kg N, 8 kg P, 8 kg K per mu. I'd rather put a little extra than see yellow leaves — a bad harvest costs more than an extra half-bag of urea.

Wheat needs water 3 times — winter water before freeze, green-up water in spring, and filling water in May. I have well access so this is fine, just the electricity bill. Spray pesticide twice — once for aphids and once for the stripe rust if I see it. Rotary tilling before sowing, plough every few years.

For summer maize after wheat, I plant Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid seed — everyone plants hybrid now, no one saves maize seed. About 2.5 kg seed per mu. I put compound fertilizer at sowing, maybe 40 kg/mu, and top-dress urea at big trumpet stage, 15 kg/mu. Total around 22 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. Maize needs less water than wheat — just 2 irrigations if rain is decent. One pesticide spray for corn borer. No-till direct seeding into the wheat stubble — that's how we all do it now, saves time and diesel.

Wheat yield I expect 450 kg/mu in a normal year, maize 550 kg/mu. My land isn't the best but it isn't the worst either.
